title: NCAA Regionals Weekend
blurb: Every D-I and D-III regional, where the nationals fields are decided, plus this week's high school championships, with live results and streams in one place.
seo: NCAA Cross Country Regionals Live Results & Streams
desc: Live results and streams for every 2026 NCAA Division I cross country regional (Nov. 13) and Division III regional (Nov. 14), plus the New Jersey Meet of Champions, the New York state meet, Nike Cross Regionals Heartland and Midwest, and this week's other high school state finals.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Mountain Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Albuquerque, NM
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. MT · Men 10K 12:00 p.m. MT
meets.why: The toughest region in the country. Men: No. 1 New Mexico, No. 2 Colorado, No. 6 BYU and No. 20 Northern Arizona. Women: No. 1 BYU, No. 6 Northern Arizona, No. 7 New Mexico, No. 9 Colorado and No. 16 Utah. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 7 New Mexico won the women’s race with 45 points as Pamela Kosgei (19:08.3), Mercy Kirarei and Marion Jepngetich went 1-2-3, with No. 6 Northern Arizona second (67) and No. 1 BYU third (81). No. 1 New Mexico also took the men’s title, 35 to 42 over No. 2 Colorado, with No. 6 BYU third (65). Texas Tech’s Titus Kimaru won the men’s race in 28:41.9.

meets.name: NCAA D-I South Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Tallahassee, FL · host Florida State · Apalachee Regional Park
meets.time: Women 6K 8:30 a.m. ET · Men 10K 9:30 a.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 4 Alabama, No. 8 Florida and No. 24 Tennessee. Women: No. 4 Alabama and No. 5 Florida. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 4 Alabama’s women won with 21 points behind a 1-2 from Caren Kiplagat (19:20.6) and Cynthia Jemutai, with No. 5 Florida second (74). Alabama’s men won too, 48 to 54 over No. 8 Florida, with No. 24 Tennessee third (120). Florida’s Kelvin Cheruiyot won the men’s race in 29:01.5, 0.7 seconds ahead of Alabama’s Dennis Kipruto.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Midwest Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Ames, IA · host Iowa State · Iowa State Cross Country Course
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. CT · Men 10K 12:00 p.m. CT
meets.why: Men: No. 3 Oklahoma State, No. 10 Iowa State, No. 22 Minnesota, No. 26 Missouri and No. 30 Tulsa. Women: No. 8 Oklahoma State, No. 20 Missouri, No. 25 Iowa State and No. 28 Minnesota. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 25 Iowa State won the women’s race with 72 points over No. 8 Oklahoma State (91), with Betty Kipkore and Rosemary Longisa second and third behind Oklahoma State’s Billah Jepkirui (19:18.9). No. 3 Oklahoma State won the men’s title 57 to 61 over No. 10 Iowa State behind a 1-2 from Brian Musau (28:47.1) and Denis Kipngetich (28:50.0).

meets.name: NCAA D-I Southeast Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Spartanburg, SC
meets.time: Women 6K 10:00 a.m. ET · Men 10K 11:00 a.m. ET
meets.why: Seven ranked women's teams: No. 2 NC State, No. 9 South Carolina, No. 12 Clemson, No. 14 Virginia Tech, No. 18 North Carolina, No. 19 Duke and No. 22 Virginia. Men: No. 9 Wake Forest, No. 15 Virginia Tech, No. 18 Eastern Kentucky and No. 23 Furman. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 2 NC State won the women’s race with 71 points as Hannah Gapes won in 18:42.2, with No. 9 South Carolina second (100) and No. 12 Clemson third (105). No. 9 Wake Forest won the men’s race with 72, and No. 18 Eastern Kentucky edged No. 15 Virginia Tech 104 to 105 for second. Louisville’s Elsingi Kipruto won the men’s race by 16.5 seconds in 28:20.3.

meets.name: NCAA D-I West Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Sacramento, CA · Arcade Creek Cross Country Course
meets.time: Women 6K 9:00 a.m. PT · Men 10K 10:00 a.m. PT
meets.why: Men: No. 5 Oregon, No. 19 Stanford and No. 27 Arizona. Women: No. 11 Oregon, No. 17 Washington State and No. 26 Washington. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 11 Oregon won the women’s race with 38 points over No. 17 Washington State (109), led by winner Diana Cherotich in 18:55.6. No. 5 Oregon’s men won with 51 points ahead of Washington (110) and No. 19 Stanford (115). Washington State’s Solomon Kipchoge won the men’s race in 28:37.6, 12 seconds ahead of teammate Evans Kurui.

meets.name: NCAA D-I South Central Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: College Station, TX · host Texas A&M
meets.time: Women 6K 9:00 a.m. CT · Men 10K 10:00 a.m. CT
meets.why: Men: No. 7 Arkansas and No. 25 Tulane. Women: No. 23 Arkansas. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 23 Arkansas won the women’s race with 51 points ahead of SMU (109) and Stephen F. Austin (113), as Texas A&M-Corpus Christi’s Elizabeth Khatevi won in 18:58.2. No. 25 Tulane beat No. 7 Arkansas 44 to 48 for the men’s title, though Arkansas freshman Nick Busienei won the race in 28:57.1, leading a 1-2 with teammate Ernest Cheruiyot.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Mid-Atlantic Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Bethlehem, PA · host Lehigh
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. ET · Men 10K 12:00 p.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 14 Georgetown and No. 17 Villanova. Women: No. 3 West Virginia, No. 24 Penn State and No. 29 Princeton. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 3 West Virginia took the top four places and won the women’s race with 19 points, led by Joy Naukot (19:19.1), with No. 24 Penn State second (83) and No. 29 Princeton third (105). No. 17 Villanova beat No. 14 Georgetown 39 to 56 for the men’s title behind a 1-2 from Bailey Habler (29:47.7) and CJ Sullivan.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Great Lakes Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: East Lansing, MI · host Michigan State · Forest Akers
meets.time: Women 6K 10:00 a.m. ET · Men 10K 11:00 a.m. ET
meets.why: Men: No. 12 Wisconsin, No. 16 Notre Dame, No. 21 Michigan State, No. 28 Michigan and No. 29 Butler. Women: No. 13 Notre Dame, No. 15 Toledo and No. 21 Northwestern. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 15 Toledo went 1-2-3 behind Karina James (19:55.2) and won the women’s race with 31 points over No. 13 Notre Dame (60). Toledo’s men also won, 59 to 66 over No. 16 Notre Dame, with Michigan State third (106) and No. 12 Wisconsin fourth (109). Butler’s William Zegarski won the men’s race in 29:55.0.

meets.name: NCAA D-I Northeast Regional Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Farmingdale, NY · host Hofstra · Bethpage State Park
meets.time: Women 6K 11:00 a.m. · Men 10K 12:00 p.m.
meets.why: Men: No. 11 Harvard and No. 13 Syracuse. Women: No. 27 Providence and No. 30 Boston College. The top two teams and the top four individuals not on those teams qualify automatically for the NCAA Championships on Nov. 21.
meets.recap: No. 13 Syracuse won the men’s title with 49 points over No. 11 Harvard (72), and host Hofstra’s Fredrick Kipkosgei won the race in 30:11.0. No. 30 Boston College edged No. 27 Providence 51 to 58 in the women’s race, with Syracuse third (77) and Syracuse’s Keira Rogan the winner in 19:46.9.

meets.name: New Jersey NJSIAA Meet of Champions Cross Country
meets.where: Holmdel, NJ · Holmdel Park
meets.why: New Jersey's fastest runners from every group race together at Holmdel. No. 1 Union Catholic's girls, who scored a perfect 15 at last week's Group meet, go for a fifth straight Meet of Champions title, with No. 19 Ridgewood also in the field. Ocean Township's Leah Starkey, the No. 2 girl in the country, ran 16:45 on this course last week. In the boys race, Union Catholic and No. 16 CBA meet again a week after Union Catholic beat CBA for the Non-Public A title, and CBA's Gavin Schmitt won that race in 15:27.

meets.name: Virginia VISAA State Cross Country Championships
meets.where: Earlysville, VA · Panorama Farms
meets.why: The state championship for Virginia's independent schools, Thursday at Panorama Farms.
meets.recap: Division I: Norfolk Academy won the boys title with 99 points over St. Stephen’s and St. Agnes (107) as Bishop Ireton’s Jason Day won in 15:36.4, and The Potomac School beat Collegiate 56-70 for the girls title as Collegiate’s Virginia Harris won in 18:43.6. Division II: North Cross swept both team titles with 39 points each, led by individual champions Finton Chaney (16:04.1) and Kaitlyn Perkins (19:27.7). Division III: Tandem Friends won the boys title (58) behind Hayes Buppert’s 15:41.0, and Trinity Academy Meadow View edged Timberlake Christian 75-79 for the girls title as Walsingham Academy’s Remington Freeman won in 18:58.2.
